name: Mitochondrial DNA Depletion Syndrome, Encephalomyopathic Form with Renal Tubulopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal consensus criteria; diagnosis based on clinical, biochemical, and genetic findings

criteria.description: Presence of progressive encephalopathy with muscle weakness and hypotonia
Evidence of renal tubular dysfunction including electrolyte imbalances and renal Fanconi syndrome
Demonstration of mitochondrial DNA depletion in affected tissues by molecular analysis
Identification of pathogenic mutations in genes associated with mitochondrial DNA maintenance (e.g., MPV17)
Elevated serum lactate and abnormal mitochondrial respiratory chain enzyme activities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical encephalomyopathy and renal tubulopathy combined with molecular evidence of mtDNA depletion or pathogenic mutations in mitochondrial maintenance genes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation including neurology, nephrology, and genetics

searchTerms: progressive brain disease with skill loss
worsening brain function and developmental decline

pathognomonic.symptomName: Renal tubular dysfunction manifesting as Fanconi syndrome
Severe mitochondrial DNA depletion in muscle or liver tissue
pathognomonic.notes: Detected via muscle or liver biopsy molecular studies
searchTerms: severe loss of mitochondrial DNA in muscle or liver
very low mitochondrial DNA in tissues
muscle or liver mitochondrial DNA shortage

common.symptomName: Electrolyte imbalances including hypophosphatemia and hypokalemia
searchTerms: electrolyte imbalances with low phosphate and potassium
abnormal blood minerals including hypophosphatemia and hypokalemia

laboratory: Elevated serum lactate and pyruvate levels
Electrolyte disturbances consistent with renal tubular dysfunction
Abnormal mitochondrial respiratory chain enzyme activities
imaging: Brain MRI showing cerebral atrophy and basal ganglia abnormalities
Renal ultrasound may show normal or mildly increased echogenicity
genetic: Pathogenic variants in MPV17 or other mitochondrial DNA maintenance genes
Mitochondrial DNA depletion demonstrated by quantitative PCR or Southern blot
other: Muscle or liver biopsy showing mitochondrial abnormalities on electron microscopy

redFlags: Rapidly progressive encephalopathy in infancy or early childhood
Severe electrolyte abnormalities refractory to supplementation
Evidence of mitochondrial DNA depletion on tissue biopsy
references: El-Hattab AW, Scaglia F. Mitochondrial DNA depletion syndromes: review and updates of genetic basis, manifestations, and therapeutic options. Neurotherapeutics. 2013;10(2):186-198.
Spinazzola A, Zeviani M. Mitochondrial DNA depletion syndromes. In: GeneReviews® [Internet]. University of Washington, Seattle; 2003-2024.
Saada A, Shaag A, Elpeleg O. Depletion of mitochondrial DNA in mitochondrial neurogastrointestinal encephalomyopathy (MNGIE). Ann Neurol. 2001;49(3):349-355.
